issues.legal_issue: The procedure for extending the time to commence commercial operations remained available to units that obtained provisional registration before the incentive scheme expired, and a later executive resolution could not curtail that opportunity without amending the statutory notification implementing the scheme.
material_facts: The scheme provided an initial period to complete a project, extensions based on the unit’s progress and difficulties, and a further opportunity to apply to the government.
The appellants obtained temporary registration before the scheme’s operative period ended and made investments in their project.
A later government resolution imposed a deadline for completing pipeline projects and barred further extensions.
The scheme had been incorporated into an entertainment-tax exemption notification issued under Section 29 of the Gujarat Entertainment Tax Act, 1977.
issues.conclusion: The extension stages of the scheme survived its operative period for units that had obtained temporary registration. The later government resolution could not curtail the opportunity promised by the scheme because it was not made into a statutory notification amending or rescinding the existing notification.
issues.legal_principle: The scheme’s text and purpose showed that the stages following provisional registration, including extension and eligibility for incentives, were intended to operate beyond the scheme’s application period for units that had crossed the threshold by obtaining temporary registration. Because the scheme’s core terms had acquired statutory status through a notification under Section 29 of the Gujarat Entertainment Tax Act, 1977, a subsequent resolution could not dilute or vary them; amendment, variation, or rescission required a statutory notification. The Court also applied the principle that a scheme should be read so as to give effect to the promised stages and eventualities for units already registered.

rule.if: incentive_scheme_appeal and unit_received_temporary_registration_before_scheme_expiry and scheme_provided_post_registration_extension_stages and scheme_terms_were_given_statutory_force and later_executive_resolution_curtailed_extension_opportunity

predicates.incentive_scheme_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging rejection of an application for time extension or related eligibility under an incentive scheme.
predicates.unit_received_temporary_registration_bef: The unit obtained temporary registration before the period for accepting new units under the scheme ended.
predicates.scheme_provided_post_registration_extens: The scheme provided registered units with further stages or opportunities to seek extensions after provisional registration.
predicates.scheme_terms_were_given_statutory_force: The scheme’s relevant terms were incorporated into a statutory notification.
predicates.later_executive_resolution_curtailed_ext: The government later issued an executive resolution that shortened or removed the extension opportunity provided by the scheme.

issues.definition: When a registered unit under an incentive scheme is promised post-registration extension stages, a later executive resolution cannot remove that opportunity if the scheme’s terms have statutory force.

issues.legal_issue: The government is bound by a clear incentive promise when a unit relies on it and materially changes its position, unless enforcing the promise would be inequitable or contrary to law.
material_facts: The scheme promised incentives and an initial period to complete a project, with possible extensions depending on the unit’s circumstances and progress.
The appellants relied on the scheme and made substantial capital investments in their project.
The State rejected the extension request in part on grounds of fiscal burden and the number of multiplexes, although the scheme had contemplated and offered the relevant opportunities.
The Court found no basis on the facts to conclude that holding the State to its promise would be inequitable.
issues.conclusion: The State was estopped from withdrawing the promised opportunity to seek extensions and could not curtail the period and opportunity provided by the scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Promissory estoppel requires a clear and unequivocal promise made with the intention that it be acted upon, and reliance on that promise that alters the promisee’s position such that it would be inequitable to permit withdrawal. The doctrine applies to government in its governmental, public, executive, administrative, and statutory functions. State of Punjab v. Nestle India Ltd., relying on Collector of Bombay v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay, Union of India v. Anglo Afghan Agencies, Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P., and Union of India v. Godfrey Philips India Ltd., states these principles and disapproves the contrary approach in Jit Ram v. State of Haryana. The doctrine cannot compel conduct contrary to law, override a statutory prohibition, or bind the legislature in its legislative functions; it also yields where the government establishes that enforcement would be inequitable. The Court also relied on S.V.A. Steel Re-Rolling Mills Ltd. v. State of Kerala concerning the State’s responsibility to consider the consequences of a policy before making assurances.

rule.if: incentive_scheme_appeal and state_made_clear_incentive_promise and unit_relied_on_promise_and_invested and no_inequity_or_legality_bar_was_established

predicates.incentive_scheme_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the rejection of a claim made under a government incentive scheme.
predicates.state_made_clear_incentive_promise: The government made a clear promise of incentives and an opportunity to seek extensions, intending eligible units to act on it.
predicates.unit_relied_on_promise_and_invested: The unit relied on the government’s promise and made substantial investments in its project.
predicates.no_inequity_or_legality_bar_was_establis: The government did not establish that enforcing the promise would be inequitable or contrary to law.

issues.definition: When the government makes a clear incentive promise, a unit relies on it by investing, and no inequity or legal bar is established, the government must honor the promise.

issues.legal_issue: When a project’s progress was seriously affected by extraordinary events and the extension request was not considered only because the authority believed it lacked power, the authority must assess the request on its merits rather than grant the extension automatically.
material_facts: An earthquake led to changes in building-safety requirements and delayed approvals for the project.
Communal riots disrupted normal life, caused workers to leave the site, and stopped construction for a period.
The appellants sought further extensions and supported their requests with progress information, investment certificates, and photographs.

The State Level Committee found the project’s progress satisfactory and the delays justifiable, but deferred consideration because it believed the later government resolution had removed its power to extend time.
The appellants had commenced commercial operations by the time of the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The State Level Committee remained competent to assess whether the appellants could justifiably claim an extension under the scheme. It was directed to make that assessment; only if the assessment favored the appellants would they be entitled to the scheme’s incentives and benefits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Clause 10 of the scheme, extension depended on consideration of the individual unit’s difficulties and progress. Once the later resolution was held ineffective to remove the promised opportunity, the authority remained competent to consider the extension request under that clause. The Court did not decide that the appellants automatically qualified for an extension or for incentives; it directed a merits assessment, with incentives following only if that assessment favored them.

predicates.incentive_scheme_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging rejection of an application for an extension under an incentive scheme.
predicates.project_delay_was_attributed_to_extraord: The unit attributed project delays to extraordinary events that disrupted approvals, construction, or the workforce.
predicates.unit_supported_extension_request_with_pr: The unit supported its extension request with information about project progress and investment.
predicates.authority_declined_merits_review_only_be: The authority did not decide the extension request on its merits because it believed it no longer had power to grant an extension.

issues.definition: When extraordinary events delayed a project, the unit supplied progress evidence, and the authority withheld a merits decision only because it believed its extension power had ended, the authority must assess the request on its merits.
